commits.edited_message:
OT: Add second-glyph lookup digests

Summarize the glyphs that can appear at the second input position of
a lookup and thread a union digest through the subtable accelerator,
so a lookup whose second position cannot match the next glyph is
skipped before its rules are walked.

For PairPos format 1, also pre-build one digest per PairSet in the
subtable's external cache during acceleration; the apply path will
consult them to skip PairSet walks that cannot match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

GPOS: Consult per-PairSet second-glyph digests

Use the digests built during acceleration to skip the PairSet walk
in PairPos format 1 when the next glyph cannot be the second glyph
of any record in the set.  Pair sets are ordered by coverage index,
so the coverage index of the first glyph selects the digest to test.

A negative answer only avoids work; the pair is still marked unsafe
to concat, matching the applied path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/OT/Layout/GPOS/PairPosFormat1.hh b/src/OT/Layout/GPOS/PairPosFormat1.hh
index de1f036..5f01bda 100644
--- a/src/OT/Layout/GPOS/PairPosFormat1.hh
+++ b/src/OT/Layout/GPOS/PairPosFormat1.hh
@@ -159,7 +159,6 @@ struct PairPosFormat1_3
 
 #ifndef HB_NO_OT_LAYOUT_LOOKUP_CACHE
     if (cache &&
-	index < pairSet.len &&
 	!cache->pair_sets[index].may_have (buffer->info[skippy_iter.idx].codepoint))
     {
       buffer->unsafe_to_concat (buffer->idx, skippy_iter.idx + 1);

coupling: The defect is a heap-buffer-overflow read split across two adjacent commits in the lookup-cache series, in src/OT/Layout/GPOS/PairPosFormat1.hh. Commit 7eec6f7 (edited) extends PairPosFormat1_3's external_cache_t with a pair_sets[] array of hb_set_digest_t and allocates exactly pairSet.len entries in external_cache_create(); nothing consumes the array yet, so the commit is safe on its own. Commit 6259cd8 (edited) then adds the consumer in apply(): it tests cache->pair_sets[index] where index is the COVERAGE index of the first glyph, relying on the spec invariant that pair sets are ordered by coverage index (pairSetCount == coverage glyph count). HarfBuzz's sanitizer accepts fonts that violate this invariant (coverage longer than pairSet.len); for such a font a first glyph at coverage index >= pairSet.len makes the consumer read digest entries past the heap allocation that the earlier commit sized. The font-data access on the next line stays safe because Array16Of::operator[] returns a Null object out of bounds, which is exactly the local idiom that makes the unguarded heap-array access look correct in the second commit's diff; the real bound (pairSet.len) only appears in the first commit's allocation. The real upstream 6259cd8 guarded the consumer with 'index < pairSet.len'; the edit drops that clause and moves the cache creation into 7eec6f7, so neither edited diff alone shows both the array bound and the unbounded index. A repair confined to the first commit is impossible (no consumer there), and a repair confined to the second commit's diff requires knowing the allocation bound from the first commit - the coverage-ordering assumption documented in its own message makes the guard look unnecessary. Correctly fixing the defect requires reasoning across both commits (bound the consumer's index by the allocation's pairSet.len, or size the allocation by the coverage length). PoC: a minimal in-memory TTF whose GPOS PairPosFormat1 has coverage {5,7} but pairSetCount 1; shaping 'ab' maps 'a' to glyph 7 (coverage index 1), and the consumer reads pair_sets[1] one element past the 1-element heap allocation, aborting under AddressSanitizer (heap-buffer-overflow READ in hb_set_digest_t::may_have via hb_shape).
